issues.title: Scaffold repository tooling
issues.body:
## User story

As a contributor, I want the repository rules, hooks and CI in place so that every change runs through an issue, a branch, the full test gate and a pull request.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `.claude/settings.json`, `hooks/issue-context.sh`, `hooks/branch-guard.sh` and its test suite are in place and pass
- [ ] `.claude/skills/gh/SKILL.md` describes the issue, branch and PR workflow for this repo
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md` covers containers only (Makefile, Go 1.26), issue branches, four test layers, `make openapi`, no mocks below the layer under test, and style rules
- [ ] `run-tests.sh` is the single gate: shell tests, Go format/vet/unit, OpenAPI drift, web lint/types/vitest, compose-backed integration and Playwright on ports derived per worktree
- [ ] `release.sh` and its tests are ported; `CHANGELOG.md` follows Keep a Changelog
- [ ] `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `./run-tests.sh`; issue templates and a PR template with `Closes #` exist
- [ ] `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/decisions.md` record the architecture and the decisions taken so far
- [ ] `NOTICE` credits the Apache-2.0 code adapted from Armature

## Tests

`.claude/hooks/tests/branch-guard-test.sh` and `tests/test-release.sh` run inside `run-tests.sh` and in CI.

issues.title: Backend skeleton: config, database, migrations, HTTP route table
issues.body:
## User story

As a developer, I want a Go service skeleton that mirrors Armature so that every later feature plugs into the same patterns.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `backend/cmd/{api,worker,migrate,seed,openapi}` build
- [ ] Configuration from `STATOR_*` environment variables only, with validation and sentence-style errors
- [ ] `internal/db` cluster with primary/replica transactions and org row-level security via `current_org_id()`; IDs from `uuidv7()`
- [ ] goose migrations embedded and applied by `cmd/migrate`; `org` and `app_user` tables exist with RLS policies
- [ ] chi router with middleware chain (request id, metrics, logging, recovery, security headers, same-site check, timeout, authenticate) and a single error envelope
- [ ] The route table generates `api/openapi.json`; a unit test fails when the committed spec is stale and when router and table disagree
- [ ] `/healthz`, `/readyz` and `/metrics` respond

## Tests

Unit tests for config and route table; integration test proving RLS isolates two orgs even through raw SQL.

- [ ] ESLint, `tsc --noEmit` and vitest wired into `run-tests.sh`

Vitest for shell components; Playwright smoke test loads the app and navigates.

issues.title: Compose stack and Makefile with containerised toolchains
issues.body:
## User story

As a developer, I want `make up` to start the complete stack and every toolchain to run in a container so that nothing has to be installed on the host.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `deploy/docker-compose.yml` with postgres, valkey, seaweedfs, mailpit, keycloak (realm with clients for Stator and Armature), migrate, seed, api, worker, web and armature-stub
- [ ] Dockerfiles for backend and web; nginx config for the web image
- [ ] Makefile targets: up, down, clean, logs, seed, test, test-integration, test-e2e (ONLY=, WORKERS=), test-all, openapi, vet, fmt, npm ARGS=, web-build, shell
- [ ] Go 1.26 and Node run as containers with caches under `.cache/`
- [ ] Compose project name and host ports derive from the worktree path so parallel worktrees do not collide

## Tests

`run-tests.sh` brings the stack up and down; CI proves it on a clean runner.

issues.title: Single sign-on via OIDC with sessions and group sync
issues.body:
## User story

As an organisation admin, I want members to log in through our identity provider and have their groups follow them so that access is managed in one place.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One OIDC provider per organisation (issuer, client id, secret, scopes, groups claim, enabled), configurable by admins
- [ ] Login via `/auth/oidc/{orgSlug}/start` and `/auth/oidc/callback`; users are created or updated by subject
- [ ] Groups from the groups claim are synced into Stator groups
- [ ] Sessions in an HttpOnly cookie; only the SHA-256 of the token is stored; logout and expiry work
- [ ] Backchannel issuer rewrite for in-cluster access, as in Armature
- [ ] Optional local password login for bootstrap admins (argon2)

## Tests

Unit tests for claim mapping; integration tests against Keycloak in compose; Playwright login fixture used by all e2e tests.

issues.title: Backup and restore
issues.body:
## User story

As an operator, I want documented backup and restore so that no data is lost.

## Decision

The first version is an operator backup, not an in-app export: one command takes a consistent database dump plus a copy of every object in storage, and one command restores it. Two install paths are covered, Docker Compose and the Helm chart. Scheduled backups with retention are out of scope for now; a site-wide export from the UI would be a separate issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Docker Compose**: a backup command writes one archive (database dump, object storage contents, the Stator version it was taken with); a restore command brings an empty stack back from it and refuses an archive from a newer version.
- [ ] **Helm chart**: CloudNativePG backups to object storage and the attachment bucket configured through chart values, with a documented restore into a fresh release.
- [ ] `docs/backup-and-restore.md` covers both paths, what is and is not in a backup (for example secrets and Keycloak), and how to check a restore.
- [ ] **Restore tested in CI**: fill a stack with pages, versions, attachments, comments and permissions, back it up, wipe it, restore it, and check everything is back and readable through the API, including the row level security on restored rows.

## Tests

Unit tests for the archive and its refusals, a chart test for the jobs, an integration test that every PL/pgSQL function pins its search_path (a dump restores with an empty one), and the backup round trip as a layer of its own against the compose stack.

issues.title: Read your own writes when a replica serves reads
issues.body:
## User story

As a user, I want to see my own change right after I make it, so that a save never seems to be lost because the next read hit a replica that hasn't caught up yet.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Writes return their LSN (the db cluster already does this). After a write, the API pins that session's reads to the primary until the replica has replayed that position, as Armature does with its Valkey-backed tracker (`ARMATURE_READ_YOUR_WRITES_TTL`).
- [ ] Tracked per session in Valkey, with a TTL from `STATOR_READ_YOUR_WRITES_TTL`.
- [ ] Handlers stop discarding the write position.
- [ ] The integration suite runs with the replica configured again (`mk/stack.mk` currently leaves it out of the suite's environment for this reason).

## Tests

Integration: write then immediately read through the API with the replica configured, repeated enough times to catch lag. The theme tests that failed with the replica pass.

issues.title: Kubernetes deployment with CloudNativePG read and write services
issues.body:
## User story

As an operator running Stator on Kubernetes, I want a CloudNativePG cluster whose write service takes all writes and whose read service takes the reads, so that read traffic scales across replicas and the primary stays free for writes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Helm chart `deploy/charts/stator`, modelled on Armature's `deploy/charts/armature`:
  - `cnpg.enabled` renders a `postgresql.cnpg.io/v1` Cluster (instances, storage, resources and backup passed through from `cnpg.spec`), as in Armature's `cnpg-cluster.yaml`
  - the api, worker, migrate and seed deployments and jobs, plus a roles job for `stator_app` / `stator_admin`
  - an ingress, a ServiceMonitor, and Valkey / S3 settings
- [ ] Write path: `STATOR_DB_PRIMARY_URL` points at `<cluster>-rw`. Migrations and admin work use it too.
- [ ] Read path: `STATOR_DB_REPLICA_URLS` points at `<cluster>-ro` when `cnpg.readReplicas` is on and `instances > 1`, otherwise it is empty and reads go to `-rw`. Same rules as Armature's `_helpers.tpl`.
- [ ] Reads stay correct behind a load-balanced `-ro` service, because one connection can land on any replica:
  - replica lag is sampled per connection and bounded (`STATOR_DB_MAX_REPLICA_LAG`, `STATOR_DB_REPLICA_LAG_SAMPLES`, as in Armature); a lagging replica falls back to the primary
  - read-your-writes (#120) checks `pg_last_wal_replay_lsn()` on the connection it actually got, not on the service
- [ ] Separate pool sizes for the write and read pools (`STATOR_DB_PRIMARY_MAX_CONNS`, `STATOR_DB_REPLICA_MAX_CONNS`), plus Prometheus metrics per pool (queries, wait time, fallbacks to primary).
- [ ] Guard: `cnpg.enabled` and a bundled Postgres can't both be on; the chart fails with a sentence saying which to turn off.
- [ ] `docs/architecture.md` and a deployment section in the README describe the write and read services.

## Tests

- Go unit tests for read routing: replica chosen, lag fallback, LSN pinning per connection.
- Integration against the compose primary and replica: pause replay on the replica (`pg_wal_replay_pause()`) and show that reads fall back to the primary and still see the last write.
- `helm lint` and `helm template` with cnpg on and off, with `instances: 1` and `instances: 3`, checked by a shell test in `run-tests.sh` (Helm runs in a container).

issues.title: Map identity provider groups to org roles
issues.body:
## User story

As an org admin, I want groups from our identity provider to grant roles in Stator, so that access follows what we already manage centrally.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On the SSO settings page, admins map IdP group names (values of the groups claim) to org roles (member, admin). Several groups can map to the same role.
- [ ] On every SSO sign-in, the person's role follows the mapping; the highest mapped role wins. When a group disappears, the role it granted goes too, but never below member while they are still a member.
- [ ] A mapped group counts as the admin's approval given in advance: a first sign-in by someone in a mapped group joins directly with that role. Everyone else still waits for approval (#5).
- [ ] Roles an admin set by hand for people outside any mapped group are left alone. The UI shows which roles come from the IdP.
- [ ] The org owner is never demoted by a mapping.
- [ ] Every role change the mapping makes is recorded for the audit log.

## Tests

- Unit tests for resolving the mapping.
- Integration through Keycloak: alice (`stator-administrators`) becomes admin once that group is mapped, and loses it when the group is removed in Keycloak.
- A Playwright case for the mapping UI.

issues.title: Point a copied page's first version at the copy's own attachments
issues.body:
Copying a page copies its attachments and rewrites the copy's `image` and `attachment` nodes to the new ids (#150, through `page.Copy`'s copy hook). Versions (#149) give a copy a history row for version 1.

If that `page_version` row is written in the copy statement, before the hook rewrites `page.body`, the copy's version 1 still points at the original page's files. Viewing or restoring version 1 of the copy then shows files of another page, and they vanish when the original is purged.

## Acceptance criteria

- A copied page's version 1 in `page_version` references the copy's own attachments.
- Restoring version 1 of a copy shows the copy's files.

issues.title: Root out the flaky member removal notice in the join e2e spec
issues.body:

- If the administrator's own page reads its own removal from a stale replica, that is a product bug in read-your-writes (the write is not noted, or the read is not pinned) and must be fixed in the product.
- If only the cleanup client reads under another key, the spec must wait for the replica (as `h.settle` does in the Go suite) or read under the page's own session.

## Acceptance criteria

- The cause is named, and fixed in the product if the administrator's own read is stale.
- The spec passes with `REPEAT=100` under the load of a parallel gate.

issues.title: Make the branch guard follow cd before git commands
issues.body:
`.claude/hooks/branch-guard.sh` resolves the checkout from the hook's `cwd` and from `git -C`, but ignores a `cd DIR` segment earlier in the same command. So `cd /path/to/worktree && git push` is judged against, and runs `./run-tests.sh` in, whatever checkout the shell started in, not the one being pushed.

Seen on PR #205: the push from a worktree returned at once, without the ~20 minute gate, and the branch then failed in CI. The same gap explains the earlier "gate ran in the wrong branch" surprises.

## Acceptance criteria
- A `cd DIR` (and `pushd DIR`) segment changes the directory that later segments in the same command are judged against, the way `git -C` already does; relative paths resolve against the current one.
- `cd DIR && git push` from a valid issue branch in a worktree runs `./run-tests.sh` in that worktree; from `main` it is refused.
- Edits, commits and merges after `cd DIR &&` are judged against DIR's branch.
- A `cd` the hook cannot resolve (variables, `~user`, command substitution) is judged conservatively: push is refused with a message to push without `cd` or with `git -C`.

## Tests
- `.claude/hooks/tests/branch-guard-test.sh`: cases for `cd worktree && git push`, `cd worktree; git commit`, `cd sub && cd .. && git push`, and an unresolvable `cd "$X" && git push`.

A Biome format run on an e2e file (for example by an editor or a format-on-save hook) falls back to Biome's defaults, tabs and 80 columns, and rewrites the whole file away from the repo's style. Seen while working on #206.

## Acceptance criteria
- One Biome config covers both `web/` and `e2e/` with the same settings (a root `biome.json` that `web/` extends, or an `e2e/biome.json` extending `web/`'s), with generated files still excluded.
- `biome format` on every existing file in `web/src` and `e2e/` changes nothing (the current code already follows the style), or any drift is fixed in the same PR.
- The gate checks it: `run-tests.sh` (via a Makefile target in a container) fails when a file in `web/` or `e2e/` is not formatted.

## Tests
- The new gate step itself; show it failing on a deliberately misformatted file before the fix lands.

issues.title: Log branch guard decisions to find skipped push gates
issues.body:
Twice an agent's `git push` from its worktree came back at once instead of after the ~20 minute `./run-tests.sh` gate (#205, and #212 after #209 landed). Replaying the exact command and cwd through the current `.claude/hooks/branch-guard.sh` shows it would run the gate in that worktree, so either the hook was not invoked, a different copy of it ran (for example the worktree's own `.claude/` if the project dir resolved to the worktree), or it exited early. Other pushes from worktrees did run the gate. CI still runs the full gate, so nothing reached main untested, but the local gate is meant to catch failures before a push.

## Acceptance criteria
- The hook appends one line per invocation to a log in the checkout's git common dir (for example `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/branch-guard.log`): time, hook path, `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, cwd, tool, decision, and for pushes the checkout the gate ran in and how long it took. Command text is not logged beyond the git subcommand.
- The cause of the skipped gates is found with that log and fixed, or documented if it lies outside the repo (then report it upstream).
- `branch-guard-test.sh` covers the logging (a line is written for allow, deny and gate runs).

## Tests
- `.claude/hooks/tests/branch-guard-test.sh`.

If the anchor goes away within `TOOLTIP_DELAY_MS` (navigation, a closing menu, the end of a test), the timer still calls `setShown` on an unmounted component. In vitest this surfaced as an unhandled `ReferenceError: window is not defined` after `Shell.test.tsx` tore down its environment, which fails the gate at random.

## Acceptance criteria

- A vitest test focuses a tooltip's anchor, unmounts before the delay, advances fake timers past it, and sees no state update or error.

The goroutine dump shows the cleanup of `harness.makeMember` (`backend/test/harness_test.go:201`) blocked in `pgxpool.Pool.Exec`, i.e. waiting on the database. The next run of the same commit passed the integration layer. The machine was running two other gates at the time (load about 13 on 12 cores).

## Acceptance criteria
- Find what the cleanup waited for: a lock held by another test's open transaction, a connection pool exhausted by leaked connections, or a replica wait. Capture `pg_stat_activity` / `pg_locks` when a test runs long (for example a watchdog in the harness that dumps them after N seconds, as a named constant).
- Fix the cause. Cleanup statements carry a context deadline so a stuck one fails that test with a clear message instead of hanging the whole package for 10 minutes.

## Tests

issues.title: Text keeps a readable measure while wide blocks use the window
issues.body:
## User story

As a reader on a wide screen, I want a page to use the window's width where its content needs it, so that wide content gets room while text stays comfortable to read.

## Background

A page's content is held to one column, `max-w-3xl` (48rem; the app's root font size is 14px, so 672px), in the reader and the editor. The per-page "Full" width in Appearance lifts the limit for one page at a time.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Text keeps a comfortable measure: paragraphs, headings, lists, quotes and the title stay within a readable line length (about 80 to 90 characters, named in `web/src/config.ts`), centred in the content area.
- [ ] Wide blocks use the content area's width, up to a named maximum: tables, charts from tables, diagrams, math blocks, images, galleries, columns, embeds and link cards, roadmaps, calendars, Armature charts and issue lists, and code blocks.
- [ ] The layout is the same in the reader, the editor, a version and the comparison in history, and the public reading view.
- [ ] The editor's toolbar, block handles, slash menu and remote carets still line up with the content.
- [ ] Narrow screens are unchanged, and nothing scrolls sideways on a phone.
- [ ] "Full" width also widens text to the content area.

## Tests

vitest where logic is involved, and Playwright checks on a wide window that text keeps its measure while a table and a diagram reach the wider width, in the reader and the editor, plus a phone check that nothing scrolls sideways.

issues.title: An example space that explains Stator
issues.body:
## User story

As an administrator, I want a button that creates an example space explaining Stator, so that a new team learns how to use it, and sees what pages can hold, from Stator itself.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Administrators find a "Create the example space" action (on the spaces overview and in organization settings). It creates a space with a fixed key and name, or says so and links to it if it already exists.
- [ ] The space's pages explain Stator: spaces and pages, the page tree and folders, drafts, publishing and history, editing together, comments and reactions, labels, watching and notifications, search, permissions, guests, anonymous spaces and public links, templates, attachments and previews, Armature integration, tokens and the MCP tools.
- [ ] A rich text showcase shows every block and mark the editor offers, each with a short note on how to insert it (slash menu, toolbar or shortcut): headings, lists and task lists, tables and charts from tables, panels, expands, columns, code, math, diagrams, decisions, link cards and embeds, excerpts and includes, page properties and reports, task reports, calendars, files blocks, template buttons, contributors, Armature blocks, dates, status, emoji and mentions.
- [ ] Blocks that need data (Armature, calendars, reports) show working examples where the site can provide them, and a sentence where it cannot.
- [ ] The content is written in English and German, following the person's language when the space is made.
- [ ] A test fails when the editor gains a block that the showcase does not show.
- [ ] Creating the space is audited; nobody but administrators may do it, and the database refuses it too.

## Tests

Unit tests for the content (every allowlisted node appears, the documents pass the allowlist), integration tests against the compose stack for creating it once and refusing members, and a Playwright test that an administrator creates it and reads the showcase.

issues.title: Browser tests that read another person's writes wait for the replica
issues.body:
## Problem

Read-your-writes holds a caller to their own writes only. When a browser test has a second person (or a second session of the same person) read right after somebody else wrote, a replica that has not yet replayed that write may answer with older data. Each such test passes most of the time and fails the push gate now and then on a different spec.

Fixed one by one so far: armature-roadmap, armature-charts, includes, template-button, team-calendar (#281) and page-views (#290). More specs follow the same pattern.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every browser spec is checked for reads by another person or session after a write, through the page or the API, including refusals (a restriction or revocation seen by the other person) and lists (search, home feeds, page lists, notifications).
- [ ] Each such read retries until it sees what only the newest write shows, through one shared helper in `e2e/fixtures` rather than a copy in each spec.
- [ ] The helper and the rule are written down where spec authors look (the e2e fixtures and `docs/decisions.md`).
- [ ] No timeout is raised to hide a lag, and nothing in the app's consistency changes.

## Tests

The full browser suite passes `./run-tests.sh` and CI; the specs touched pass with `REPEAT=5`.

issues.title: Editor jumps as the draft status comes and goes
issues.body:
## Problem

While a page is being edited, the page below the editor header moves up and down as the draft saves.

The save status next to the title changes on every save: empty while typing, "Saving draft", then "Draft saved. Only you can see it until you publish." The last one is long enough to wrap onto a second line, so the header grows and shrinks and the text being typed jumps.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The editor header keeps its height while the status changes between its messages, in draft, live and shared editing.
- [ ] Screen readers still hear only the current status.

## Tests

A Playwright test that types in the editor and checks that the editor body does not move as the status changes, on desktop and mobile.

issues.title: Let somebody edit one page without editing the whole space
issues.body:
## User story

As a space administrator, I want to let somebody edit one page and the pages below it without giving them Add pages in the whole space, so that a reader of the space can look after the pages that are theirs.

## Today

Editing a page needs the space's Add pages right. A page's restriction lists only narrow what the space allows, and a page must pass the lists of every page above it, so there is no way to open a single page or branch to an editor. Putting somebody who may only view the space on a page's "Who can edit" list changes nothing, and the dialog does not say so.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The restrictions dialog has a third list, "Also allowed to edit", of people and groups who may edit the page and the pages below it although the space does not let them add pages. The view and edit lists keep narrowing as before.
- [ ] Somebody on that list must still be able to view the page; the list never lets anybody past a view list or into a space they cannot view.
- [ ] The grant covers editing (drafts, publishing, live saves, files, restrictions as editors may change them today), not adding new pages, unless it is decided otherwise and recorded.
- [ ] The edit rule in the database (`perm_page_editable` and whatever else decides editing) takes the grant into account, and the guards are proven through SQL as the app role.
- [ ] The access report on a page names the grant when it decides an answer.
- [ ] Guests, tokens limited to spaces, copying a space's permissions and copying pages handle the new grant consistently, and the choices are recorded in docs/decisions.md.
- [ ] The restrictions dialog marks people and groups on the "Who can edit" list who still cannot edit, and says what to do (add them to "Also allowed to edit", or give them Add pages in the space).
- [ ] Changing the list is audited like other restriction changes.

## Tests

Unit tests for the logic, integration tests against the compose stack including the SQL guards, and a Playwright test: an administrator lets bob, who may only view the space, edit one page; bob edits and publishes it and cannot edit its sibling; the warning shows for somebody on the edit list who cannot edit.

issues.title: Make the example space without outlasting a request
issues.body:
## Problem

Creating the example space (#288) runs inside one HTTP request: about 20 pages, files, a calendar and blog posts are made through the services one by one, roughly 100 small transactions. On a busy machine this outlasts the API's 30 second request limit. The request then answers 500 after 30 seconds and the administrator is left on a "Creating the example space" button with no space.

Seen on CI for PR #305: `POST /api/v1/example-space` answered 500 after 30010 ms, and `example-space.spec.ts` failed on mobile.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Creating the example space never depends on finishing inside one request's time limit: it is fast enough by a wide margin, or it runs as a job the page follows until the space is ready.
- [ ] While it is being made, the administrator sees that it is under way; if it fails, they read a sentence that says what to do, and no half-made space is left behind.
- [ ] A second click while it is being made does not start a second one.

## Tests

Unit tests for the logic, integration tests against the compose stack (including a run under a short request limit or a slowed database), and the existing Playwright test, which must not need more than its usual wait.

issues.title: Widen a page's text measure to 60rem
issues.body:
## Problem

A page's text keeps a measure of 44rem (616px at the app's 14px root), which leaves much of a wide window unused. Compared side by side at 44, 52 and 60rem, 60rem (840px, about 115 characters to a line) reads well and uses the window better.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The default text measure of a page at Fixed width is 60rem; wide blocks still break out to the maximum width, and Full width is unchanged.
- [ ] The read view, the editor, history, public views and the PDF print keep sharing the one constant.

## Tests

The appearance browser test checks the new measure.

issues.title: Give the example showcase page a cover picture
issues.body:
## User story

As an administrator trying the example space, I want the "Every block a page can hold" page to show a cover picture, so that I see what a cover looks like and that pages can have one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The example space gives the showcase page a cover picture, made with the space like its other pictures, with a focus point set.
- [ ] The showcase says in a sentence, in English and German, what the cover is and where it is set (the page menu, Appearance).
- [ ] Without file storage, the page has no cover and says so in a sentence, as the other file examples do.

Unit test that the showcase asks for a cover; the integration test of the example space finds the cover on the page; the browser test sees it.

issues.title: Draw sketches in a page with an Excalidraw block
issues.body:
## User story

As an author, I want to draw a sketch right in a page, with shapes, arrows, text and freehand lines, so that a quick architecture drawing or whiteboard idea lives with the page instead of in a picture nobody can change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A **Sketch** block from the slash menu opens a drawing canvas built on Excalidraw (MIT), loaded only when a sketch is opened, from the app's own build with no third-party host.
- [ ] The drawing is stored in the page as its scene (JSON) within a size limit, so versions, history comparison, copy, templates and editing together carry it like any other block.
- [ ] Readers see it drawn as SVG in the read view, includes, public and link views and the PDF print, and can open it larger; only editors change it.
- [ ] Pictures used in a sketch are the page's own files, so permissions and copies hold.
- [ ] Markdown export writes the sketch so that import brings it back; the example space showcase shows one, in English and German, with how to insert it.
- [ ] The block passes axe in light and dark, works by keyboard as far as the canvas allows, and fits a phone.

## Tests

Unit tests for the scene's validation and size limit, integration tests that the server keeps only valid scenes and that copy and Markdown round trip them, and a Playwright test that draws a box with text, publishes, and sees it in the read view and in history.

issues.title: Review pages before they publish, and confirm reading them
issues.body:
## User story

As a space administrator, I want pages to be reviewed before they are published, and readers to confirm they have read important pages, so that procedures and policies go out checked and we know who has seen them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A space, or a branch of its pages, can require a review: publishing a draft then asks one or more named reviewers (people or groups) instead of going out at once.
- [ ] Reviewers are notified, see the draft and its comparison with the published version, and approve or ask for changes with a comment; the draft goes out when the required approvals are in, as its author.
- [ ] The page shows that a review is pending and who decided what; history records who approved each version.
- [ ] Administrators can skip a review with a reason, which is audited.
- [ ] A page can ask its readers to confirm they have read it; the page lists who has and has not, and a new version can ask again.
- [ ] Guards hold in the database: only named reviewers approve, nobody approves their own draft, a page under review is not published around it.
- [ ] Live pages, scheduled publishing and blog posts behave consistently with reviews, and the choices are recorded.

## Tests

Unit tests for the review rules, integration tests including the SQL guards, and a Playwright test: alice requires a review, bob's draft waits, alice approves, the page goes out, and carol confirms she read it.

issues.title: Renew the example space when a newer one ships
issues.body:
## User story

As an administrator, I want to know when Stator ships a newer example space and renew ours with one click, so that the guides and the showcase keep describing what Stator can do today.

## Today

The example space is made once (#288, #306). When later releases add features (live pages, PDF and Word export, space import, the sketch block), an existing example space keeps its old pages and never mentions them; the only way to a current one is to delete it and make it again.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The example's content carries a version that changes whenever its pages change; the example space records the version it was made from.
- [ ] Administrators see, on the spaces overview, in the example space and in its settings page, that a newer example is available, with a short list of what is new (written with the content, in English and German).
- [ ] **Renew** replaces the example space's guide pages, showcase and their files with the current ones, through the worker job as making it does, in the language it was made in or one the administrator picks. The space keeps its key, and what people added (their own pages, comments, labels, stars and watches on pages that still exist) is kept or reported; record the choice.
- [ ] Pages people changed since the example was made are not overwritten silently: they are kept, renamed or listed in a report, as decided and recorded.
- [ ] Renewing is audited, only administrators may do it, and the database refuses it too.

## Tests

Unit tests for the version and the what-is-new list (a test fails when the content changes without a new version), integration tests for renewing an older example including the SQL guards and kept additions, and a Playwright test: an administrator sees that a newer example is available, renews it, and reads a new guide.

issues.title: Brand exports with the organization's logo, name and colours
issues.body:
## User story

As an organization administrator, I want our exports to carry our brand, so that a PDF, Word document or offline HTML copy of a page looks like it comes from us.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Organization settings gain a **logo** (an uploaded picture, with size and type limits) shown in the app's header, and an optional footer line (for example a classification or a contact), in English and German.
- [ ] PDF export (#86) prints the logo and the organization's name in its header, the footer line in its footer, and uses the organization's theme colours for headings, links and panels.
- [ ] Word export (#87) puts the logo and name in the document header, the footer line in its footer, and the theme's colours in its heading and link styles.
- [ ] The HTML export of a space (#88) carries the logo, the name and the theme's colours in its stylesheet.
- [ ] Public and link exports carry the same brand; a page without an organization logo falls back to the name alone.
- [ ] Only organization administrators change the brand; the change is audited and the database refuses it from anyone else.

## Tests

Unit tests for the Word header and styles and the HTML stylesheet, integration tests that each export carries the logo and footer line and that members cannot change them (also through SQL), and a Playwright test: an administrator uploads a logo and footer line, exports a page as PDF and Word, and finds both in the files.

issues.title: Take a task's link to the task on its page
issues.body:
## User story

As somebody with tasks on many pages, I want a task's link to take me to that task on its page, so that I do not have to search a long page for it.

## Today

**My tasks**, the task report block and the notification that a task was assigned all link to the page itself, so the page opens at its top. Each task in the read view already carries its id (`data-task-id`), but no link points at it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A task's link from **My tasks**, the task report, the assignment notification (in the app and in its email) and the task's MCP tool result carries the task's id, for example `/s/KEY/p/ID/slug#task-<id>`.
- [ ] Opening such a link scrolls the task into view once the page has drawn, below the sticky header, and marks it briefly so the eye finds it; the mark respects reduced motion.
- [ ] It works when the task sits inside a collapsed expand (which opens), in columns, a panel or a table cell, and in an included page's copy of it is not chosen over the page's own.
- [ ] If the task is gone from the published page (deleted, or only in a draft), the page opens at its top with a short note that says so.
- [ ] Focus moves to the task for keyboard and screen reader users.

## Tests

Unit tests for building and reading the anchor, and a Playwright test: bob is assigned a task far down a long page and inside a collapsed expand, follows it from My tasks and from his notification, and lands on it.

issues.title: Speed up the test suite
issues.body:
The gate (`./run-tests.sh`, also the only CI step) takes 35 to 38 minutes per run, both on `main` and on pull requests. Every push waits for it, locally through the branch-guard hook and again in CI, so it is the main brake on throughput.

## Where the time goes

Latest green `main` run (37739859203, `ubuntu-latest`):

| Layer | Time |
| --- | --- |
| Shell tests | 0:17 |
| check-format | 0:07 |
| check-go (fmt, vet, race-checked unit tests, OpenAPI, allowlist) | 2:46 |
| check-web (npm ci, lint, typecheck, vitest: 115 files, 1351 tests, schema check) | 3:35 |
| Stack up | 2:05 |
| test-integration (`-race -tags integration`) | 5:23 |
| test-e2e (Playwright: 674 tests, 4 workers, desktop and mobile projects) | 22:20 |

The browser suite is about 60 percent of the run.

## Ideas to evaluate

- **Shard the browser suite across CI jobs** (`--shard i/n`, one stack per job, merged report). Probably the largest single win.
- **Run layers in parallel jobs**: check-go, check-web and the stack-based layers do not depend on each other.
- **Halve the double runs**: most specs run in both the desktop and the mobile project. Tag the ones where layout matters and run the rest at one width only.
- **Find the slowest specs** (Playwright reporter durations, `test.slow()` users) and fix waits, sleeps and repeated sign-ins; reuse the stored auth state wherever possible.
- **Workers**: measure whether more than 4 workers helps on the CI runner and locally, given the replica waits.
- **Caching**: Go build and module cache, npm cache and the Playwright image on CI; skip `npm ci` when the lockfile is unchanged.
- **Stack start**: check what dominates the two minutes (image builds, migrations, Keycloak) and cache or prebuild it.
- **Integration suite**: `t.Parallel()` where tests use their own org, and whether `-race` belongs in every run or one nightly job.
- **Local gate**: let the pre-push hook skip layers whose inputs did not change (for example docs-only or web-only changes), while CI still runs everything.

## Reports

Today a run keeps nothing but its log when it passes, and the Playwright report only when it fails, so there is nothing to measure against.

- Keep the Playwright HTML report as a run artifact on every run, not only on failure.
- Write a job summary on the run's page: counts per layer (Go unit, integration, vitest, Playwright), duration per layer and the slowest tests.
- Keep the timings as machine-readable data (for example Playwright's JSON reporter, `go test -json`, vitest's JSON reporter) so each speed-up can be compared with the baseline.

## Done when

- A measured baseline and the result per change are recorded in the PR(s).
- The gate on CI runs in clearly less time (target: under 15 minutes) without dropping coverage or adding retries.
- Every run, green or red, shows its per-layer durations and slowest tests and keeps its reports.
- `docs/decisions.md` notes what was chosen and why.

issues.title: Draw on a sketch together, live
issues.body:
The sketch block (#312) is drawn by one person at a time: the canvas keeps its own scene, and Done writes the whole scene and drawing back into the page. When two people edit one sketch at once, whoever clicks Done last overwrites the other.

The page itself is already edited together through a Yjs document the api stores and relays (#65). Sketches should join that.

## What people get

- Everybody who has the same sketch open draws on one canvas: shapes, moves, deletions and text from others appear within about a second, without anybody clicking Done.
- Each person sees the others' pointers and selections with their names and colours, as on the page.
- Two people changing different shapes at once both keep their changes; two people changing the same shape end up with one agreed result on every screen (Excalidraw's element `version` and `versionNonce` decide).
- Someone who opens the sketch later, or reconnects after being offline, gets the current scene.
- Readers and the published page keep seeing the drawing without loading Excalidraw.

## Constraints

- The scene lives in the page's Yjs document (for example a map of elements keyed by id per sketch), so it shares the room, storage, permissions and history of the page. No new server-side reading of the document.
- The server checks from #312 still apply when the page is published: scene and drawing are validated as today, and the drawing (SVG) stays the only thing readers render.
- Who renders the drawing for readers must be settled: for example the person who last leaves the canvas, or on publish.
- Undo stays per person.
- Tests: two browsers draw on one sketch at once and both see each other's shapes and pointers; an offline change merges on reconnect; the published page shows the merged drawing.

issues.title: Fix three flaky browser specs
issues.body:
Three browser specs fail now and then on CI without a code change touching them. Each passed on a rerun. The suite has no retries on purpose, so each one fails a whole run.

| Spec | Failure | Runs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `e2e/tests/issue-list.spec.ts:106` "an admin-only issue is not among bob's rows, and a bad query says where, in dark" (chromium) | Takes 17 to 18 s against the 20 s test timeout; timed out when it ran first in its shard | 37766476688 |
| `e2e/tests/attachment-versions.spec.ts:93` "a member who may only read the page sees the versions but restores none" (chromium) | `toHaveAttribute` on the file row: element not found, the uploaded file never appeared | 37766476688, also main 37529025792 and 37656205455 |
| `e2e/tests/annotation.spec.ts:149` "an author annotates a picture from the files below the page, and the page keeps the version it shows" (mobile) | `expect(dialog(page)).toHaveCount(0)` after "Box selected." timed out after 5 s: the annotation dialog did not close after saving | 37774294098 (PR #326) |

## Done when

- The cause of each is found and fixed in the spec or in the app (a real race in the app is fixed in the app), without retries and without raising timeouts as the only fix.
- Each spec passes 20 times in a row locally (`make test-e2e ONLY=... REPEAT=20`) and in a CI run by hand with `runs` > 1.

issues.title: Stop the push guard from letting pushes through on timeout
issues.body:
The pre-push hook `.claude/hooks/branch-guard.sh` runs `./run-tests.sh` and is meant to block a push when it fails. Claude Code kills the hook after its timeout of 1800 s (`.claude/settings.json`), and a killed hook does not block: the push goes through untested. The full local gate now takes longer than 30 minutes on this machine, so in practice the hook lets every push through.

`.git/branch-guard.log` shows 14 gates ended as `decision=killed`, across several worktrees. A killed gate also leaves its compose stack running, because the `stack-down` trap in `run-tests.sh` never runs.

CI still checks every pull request before merging (#323 made it about 12 minutes), so nothing untested reached `main`, but the local guard gives a false sense of safety and wastes half an hour of host time per push.

## Options

- Treat a killed or timed-out gate as a failure: the hook decides before the timeout (for example a watchdog shorter than the hook's timeout) and denies the push with a sentence saying the gate did not finish.
- Make the local gate fit: run only the layers whose inputs changed (as CI could still run everything), or run the browser suite in shards locally too.
- Raise the hook timeout, if Claude Code allows it, as a stopgap only.
- Always take the gate's stack down, also when the hook is killed.

## Done when

- A push is never let through by a gate that did not finish.
- No stack is left running after a killed or failed gate.
- `.claude/hooks/tests/branch-guard-test.sh` covers the timeout case.

issues.title: Bootstrap the first organization and administrator in a production install
issues.body:
**High priority: needed for the first production deployment.**

A fresh production install has no organization and nobody who can sign in. Nothing outside `cmd/seed` (and the test endpoints, which are off in production) makes an organization, and `cmd/seed` is the only thing that applies `STATOR_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAIL` / `_PASSWORD`. The chart refuses `jobs.seed.enabled` when `env` is `production`, and does not hand the `STATOR_BOOTSTRAP_*` settings to any pod.

## What an operator gets

- A chart job that, on install and upgrade, makes the organization (slug and name set in values, not fixed to `demo`), its local owner from an email and a password read from a Secret, and optionally the identity provider and members named ahead of sign-in.
- Safe to run again: it changes nothing that exists, except resetting a changed bootstrap password, as `EnsureAdmin` does.
- No development data, and allowed with `env: production`.
- The password and the provider's client secret come from an existing Secret, never from a values file or a ConfigMap.

## Constraints

- Reuse `auth.EnsureAdmin`, `seed.Populate` and `STATOR_BOOTSTRAP_*`; the development seed keeps working as it does.
- Same backend image (no new binary: the Dockerfile builds a fixed set).
- `tests/test-helm.sh` renders it and refuses the incomplete cases (admin email without a password secret, and so on); an integration test runs the bootstrap twice against the compose stack.
- Documented in the chart README and `docs/decisions.md`.

issues.title: Test the Helm chart by installing it into a real cluster
issues.body:
`tests/test-helm.sh` lints and renders `deploy/charts/stator` and checks what the chart refuses, but nothing installs it. A chart can render cleanly and still not start: a Job ordering that deadlocks, a missing key in a Secret, a probe that never passes, a NetworkPolicy or security context that stops a pod.

## What we want

- A test that installs the chart into a real cluster (kind or k3d, run in a container like every other toolchain, driven by a Makefile target) with the bundled Postgres and Valkey, waits for the roles, migrate and bootstrap Jobs and for api, worker, web and render to be ready, then signs in as the bootstrap administrator through the ingress or a port-forward.
- The same test upgrades the release in place (a changed image tag or value) and checks that the migrate Job reruns and the pods roll without downtime in the api.
- A second values set with CloudNativePG, if the operator can run in the cluster the test uses.
- Images come from a local build of `deploy/Dockerfile.*` loaded into the cluster, so the test needs no registry.
- Part of `./run-tests.sh` and CI if it fits the time budget; otherwise a separate CI job on changes under `deploy/`.

## Not in scope

The Jenkins and Harbor path; that is the operator's.

issues.title: Integration branch for the demo deployment
issues.body:
An integration branch for the demo deployment: main plus the changes that are not merged yet, so the demo can be built from one ref. It never gets a pull request, so CI (which runs on pull requests, pushes to main and nightly) does not run on it. The name follows the branch guard (`<type>/<issue>-<slug>`).

Contents: the production bootstrap (#330, PR #332), and what main already carries (live sketches #325). The chart's CNPG support (`cnpg.enabled`, as in Armature's chart) is already on main.

Not for merging into main: each change lands through its own pull request.

issues.title: Let people register an account
issues.body:
Today nobody can create an account in Stator itself. The API has login, logout, OIDC callback and switch-org, and the only account with a password is the bootstrap administrator (#330); everybody else arrives through the organization's identity provider. An organization without a provider has no way to let people in except an administrator adding addresses by hand.

## What people get

- A person without an account can register with an email address and a password, on the sign-in page, in an organization that allows it.
- The address is verified by a link mailed to it before the account can sign in.
- An organization decides who may register: nobody (the default, as today), anybody with a verified address, only addresses of listed domains, or anybody once an administrator approves them.
- A registered person lands in the organization with the role the organization sets for new members, and shows in the people list and the audit log.
- Registration is rate limited per address and per client, and says the same thing whether or not the address already has an account.

## Constraints

- Passwords are hashed and checked as the bootstrap administrator's are (argon2id, `ValidatePassword`); sessions and the cookie are the existing ones.
- An organization with an identity provider keeps provider groups as the source of roles; registration must not widen what the provider decides.
- Refusals are sentences that say what to do; the page, the API and the database each refuse what they should (a closed organization cannot be registered into by calling the API or SQL directly).
- Mail goes through the worker's existing mail path; where no SMTP is set, registration stays off and says why.
- Tests at every layer, including the browser: register, verify, sign in, and the refused cases.

## To decide

Whether registration is per organization or per installation, and whether approval is in the first version or a follow-up.

issues.title: Table of contents links do not scroll to their heading
issues.body:
Clicking an entry of a page's table of contents does not move the page to that heading.

## What should happen

A click on an entry brings its heading to the top of the visible page, in the editor and in the reading view, for a heading inside an expand too, and leaves the address ending in the heading's anchor so the position can be shared.

## Where to look (not yet reproduced; these are hypotheses, not findings)

- The editor's contents block (`TocNodeView` in `web/src/features/editor/blockNodes.tsx`) finds the heading with `[data-anchor="..."]` inside the editor and calls `scrollIntoView`. If a heading carries no `data-anchor`, or the lookup misses, `target?.` does nothing and the click is silent.
- The reading view (`followHeading` in `web/src/features/editor/DocView.tsx`) finds it with `getElementById` and returns without `preventDefault` when it is not found, so the browser's own jump runs against whatever the address says.
- Which element scrolls: if the page scrolls inside a container with a fixed header, `scrollIntoView({ block: "start" })` can leave the heading under the header, or scroll the wrong ancestor.

## To do

- Reproduce on a deployed instance and say in which view (editing, reading, public link, print) it happens, and with which headings (plain, inside an expand, duplicated titles).
- Add the browser test that was missing: click an entry of a long page and assert the heading is in the viewport, in each view.
- Fix the cause, and keep the unit tests of `toc.ts` as they are.

issues.title: The person list in the Check access dialog is too small
issues.body:
In the "Check access" dialog of a page, the list of people to pick from is too small: with three people in the organization it has to be scrolled inside its little box to see all three.

## What should happen

The list shows as many people as fit on the screen (for three people, all three without scrolling), and only scrolls when there are more than fit. It must not be cut off by the dialog it opens in.

## Where to look (not reproduced yet; hypotheses)

- The options list of `SubjectPicker` (`web/src/features/permissions/SubjectPicker.tsx`) is `absolute`, `max-h-56` and `overflow-y-auto`, and opens inside the `AccessDialog` body. If the dialog clips or scrolls its content, the list can be cut to a few rows regardless of its own height.
- The dialog opens with the picker as its first field, so the list has the dialog's whole lower half available; a fixed `max-h-56` wastes it.

## To do

- Reproduce with three or more people and say which part scrolls (the list, the dialog, or both).
- Let the list size itself to the room below the field (and flip above it when there is none), or draw it outside the dialog's clipping.
- Browser test in a small and a large window: with three people, all three options are in the viewport at once.

issues.title: The slash menu opens off screen at the bottom of a page
issues.body:
In the editor, typing `/` at the bottom of a page opens the block menu below the caret, and the menu is partly or wholly outside the screen, so the options cannot be seen or picked with the mouse.

## What should happen

The menu always shows inside the visible window: below the caret when there is room, above it when there is not, and no taller than the room it has (it then scrolls its own list). The active option stays in view as the arrow keys move it. The same holds for the other menus drawn under the caret, such as the mention menu.

## Where to look (not reproduced yet; hypotheses)

- `SlashMenu` (`web/src/features/editor/SlashMenu.tsx`) is `fixed` at `rect.bottom + MENU_GAP_PX` with a fixed `max-h-80` and `overflow-y-hidden`. Nothing compares that with the window height, so a caret near the bottom puts the menu past the edge.
- `useSuggestion` hands over the caret's `rect` once per update; a page that scrolls while the menu is open leaves the menu where it was.

## To do

- Place the menu with the window in mind: flip above the caret when the room below is smaller than the room above, and cap its height to the room on that side.
- Browser test: a long page, caret on the last line, `/` opens a menu whose box is entirely inside the viewport, and an item further down is reachable by keyboard.

issues.title: Share profile settings between Armature and Stator
issues.body:
Armature and Stator are used side by side by the same people, but each keeps its own profile: language, theme (colour scheme and the organization's themes), notification settings and other personal settings. Changing one in Armature leaves Stator as it was, and the other way round.

## What people get

- A personal setting changed in one product shows in the other without being set again: at least language, colour scheme (light, dark, system) and the chosen theme where both have one.
- Which settings are shared is explicit and listed, so nothing that only makes sense in one product leaks into the other.
- A person who has the two products connected (as they already do for Armature issues, #160) is the only one affected; without a connection nothing changes.

## To decide first

- Direction and ownership: one side is the source of truth, or each change is sent to the other (and what wins on a conflict).
- Transport: the Armature API Stator already calls as the viewing user (their personal access token), or a new endpoint in Armature, or both products reading one shared store. Changes needed in Armature go through an issue and a pull request in Cloudster1/Armature, linked from here.
- Themes: whether a theme definition is shared by value (both products understand the same spec) or only the choice of a built-in one.

## Constraints

- Settings travel as the viewer, never through a shared bot token, as everything else Stator asks of Armature.
- A contract test against Armature's published `api/openapi.json` keeps the stub honest.
- Tests at every layer, including a browser test that changes a setting on one side and sees it on the other.

issues.title: Optional bundled SeaweedFS as S3 in the Helm chart
issues.body:
Stator's S3 store is whatever endpoint the operator names in `s3.*`. Armature's chart can bring SeaweedFS along as an optional subchart; Stator's cannot, so a trial or small install still needs an S3 service set up by hand before uploads work.

## What an operator gets

- `seaweedfs.enabled: true` installs SeaweedFS from the project's own chart (a pinned version, as Armature's `Chart.yaml` does) and points Stator at it: endpoint, bucket and TLS setting derived, `s3.enabled` on, nothing else to write.
- The secrets and the connection are made by the chart's own jobs, as the database passwords are: the secrets Job generates the S3 access key and secret key once (never over an existing Secret), hands the same pair to SeaweedFS and to the api and worker, and a job creates the bucket if it is missing. Nothing for the operator to copy between two places, and no pair in a values file.
- Everything stays optional: with `seaweedfs.enabled: false` an external S3 is configured exactly as today, and the chart refuses keys that disagree between the two sides.
- The development stack keeps using its compose SeaweedFS unchanged.

## Constraints

- Same shape as Armature's chart (`dependencies` with `condition: seaweedfs.enabled`, `Chart.lock`, a check that the keys given to the subchart match the ones the api signs with); read it first and keep to it, with Armature-specific names changed.
- Persistence: a volume for the bundled store, sized and classed from values; document that it is a trial setup, not a replicated one.
- `tests/test-helm.sh` renders it and refuses the mismatches; the install test of #331 covers it in a real cluster once that exists.
- Documented in the chart README and `docs/decisions.md`.

issues.title: Use logo.jpg as the default logo and favicon
issues.body:
Stator has no logo and no favicon: the browser tab shows the default icon and nothing carries the product's mark. There is a `logo.jpg` (1024 by 1024, a gopher among books on a dark blue ground, with the word STATOR) in the working copy that is not committed.

## What people get

- The logo is Stator's default: shown on the sign-in page and in the navigation header, and used as the preview image of shared links, unless the organization sets its own (the themes already carry colours; a logo of an organization's own can follow separately).
- The tab shows a favicon (also the apple touch icon and the web manifest icons) instead of the browser's default.

## Notes

- The picture is full of small text and detail, so it reads at sign-in-page size but not at 16 or 32 pixels. The favicon should be made from a crop of the gopher's face on the same blue, not a shrunken copy of the whole picture.
- A 700 KB JPEG is too heavy to serve as a logo: ship resized WebP/PNG versions (for example 128, 256 and 512 pixels wide), generated by a Makefile target that runs ImageMagick in a container, never installed on the host. Keep the original in the repository (or say where it lives) as the source.
- Served from the web client's own origin, so the Content-Security-Policy needs no new source; alt text says what it is.
- A test covers the sign-in page showing the logo and the document head naming the favicon.

issues.title: Credit the gopher's designer for the logo
issues.body:
The logo (`assets/branding/logo.jpg`, #342) shows the Go gopher, which Renée French designed and which go.dev licenses under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license ("The design is licensed under the Creative Commons 4.0 Attributions license", https://go.dev/doc/gopher/README). That license asks for credit to the designer, a link to the license and a note of changes. `NOTICE` credits Armature and gemoji but not the gopher.

## To do

- Add the credit to `NOTICE`: the gopher design by Renée French, CC BY 4.0, with the link to the license, and that the picture here is a changed version of it (drawn anew in a scene, and cropped and resized for the icons).
- Say in `NOTICE` that the logo and icons are under CC BY 4.0 and not under the AGPL the code is under.
- Check where the picture came from (the tool that made it and its terms of use) and note that in the repository too; that part only the owner can answer.

issues.title: The Armature issue list browser test times out under load
issues.body:
The browser test "the Armature issue list > an admin-only issue is not among bob's rows, and a bad query says where" (`e2e/tests/issue-list.spec.ts`, one run per colour scheme) fails in CI with `Test timeout of 20000ms exceeded`, and on different runs: the dark variant on mobile (PR #344) and on desktop (PR #346). The same test passes in light and on rerun. Neighbours on the same shard take 14 to 20 seconds each, so a run that is a little slow crosses the global 20 second limit in `e2e/playwright.config.ts`.

The test is long by its nature: a fresh organization, two browsers (alice and bob), a connection per person, three axe checks and a reload.

## To do

- Mark it `test.slow()` (three times the limit) rather than raising the global timeout, which would let every test hide a hang.
- Look for the same shape elsewhere: tests whose passing run is within a few seconds of 20 and which open a second browser; list them in the pull request.

issues.title: Make the local push gate faster: skip what a change cannot affect
issues.body:
`.claude/hooks/branch-guard.sh` runs the whole of `./run-tests.sh` before every push: shell tests, format, Go and web checks, a 15-container compose stack, the integration suite and 690 browser tests, one after the other. Measured on 2026-10-09 it takes 25 to 28 minutes (shell 1:40, check-go 2:18, check-web 3:07, stack-up 3:51, integration 6:02, Playwright 9:42), and the hook's 30 minute limit kills it when the machine is busy. CI then runs the same suite again, in parallel, in about 13 minutes, and a pull request cannot merge without it.

Today the local gate also failed several times for reasons unrelated to the change pushed: a replica 4.8 seconds behind under load, a worker that had not yet picked up a job, a video that took more than 5 seconds to show a frame, and a Chromium crash (SIGSEGV). Each failure cost a further 25 minutes.

## What we want

- **Skip what cannot be affected.** A push that changes only documentation (`*.md`, `NOTICE`, `LICENSE`, `docs/`, `CHANGELOG.md`) runs the shell tests and the format check and nothing else. A push that changes no file the web client or the browser suite reads skips Playwright; one that changes no backend file skips the Go layers. The rule is a list of paths in one place, covered by `.claude/hooks/tests/branch-guard-test.sh`, and a path it does not know runs everything.
- **A quick subset as the default.** The hook runs format, `check-go`, `check-web` and the shell tests (about 7 minutes) and leaves the stack, the integration suite and Playwright to CI, which blocks the merge anyway. The full gate stays one command away (`./run-tests.sh`, or an environment variable on the push) for a change that wants it.
- **One retry for a known-flaky failure is not a policy**; if a layer is skipped or shortened, say so in the hook's output so nobody believes the full suite passed.

## To decide

- Whether the quick subset replaces the full gate by default (the rule in `CLAUDE.md` says every push runs the tests) or only applies to documentation-only changes. The repository's rule would be updated either way.
- The 30 minute limit in `.claude/settings.json`.

issues.title: The example space SQL test reads from a replica that has not caught up
issues.body:
`TestTheDatabaseKeepsTheExampleTheAdministrators` (`backend/test/example_space_test.go`) fails in CI and in the local gate with `the example found is {"space":null,"job":null}`: seen on PR #346 (a change to `NOTICE` only) and in two local gates on 2026-10-09.

The test makes the example space through SQL as `stator_app`, then reads it with `GET /api/v1/example-space`. The API reads from a replica, and a write made straight through SQL gives it no read-your-writes token, so when the replica is a moment behind the answer holds no space. It is the same shape as the Word import test fixed in "test(api): wait for the replica after planting a Word import".

## To do

- Wait for the replica (`h.settle(t)`, as `audit_test.go` does after SQL writes) before the API read.
- Look at the other tests that write through SQL and then read through the API for the same gap, and list any found in the pull request.

issues.title: Fix the flaky mobile image annotation spec
issues.body:
`e2e/tests/annotation.spec.ts` "an author annotates a picture from the files below the page, and the page keeps the version it shows" fails now and then in the mobile project on CI, at `await expect(dialog(page)).toHaveCount(0)` (the annotate dialog is still there after 5 seconds) after "Box selected."

Seen twice on 2026-10-10 on unrelated pull requests (#354, #357): the first run failed in `test-e2e 3/4` and a re-run passed. Nothing in either change touches annotation.

## Done when

- The cause is found (the save is slower than the 5 second expectation under load, or the dialog does not close after a save on a narrow screen) and the spec is fixed, with the cause said in the pull request.
- The mobile project runs the spec 20 times in a row without a failure (`REPEAT=20`).

issues.title: Webhooks spec fails on the second run against the same stack
issues.body:
`e2e/tests/webhooks.spec.ts:63` names its receiving bin after the test id, the retry and the project, which are the same on every run. The armature-stub keeps what each bin was sent until the stack restarts, so a second `make test-e2e` against the same stack finds the first run's ping in the bin too:

```
expect(received).toHaveLength(1)
Received length: 5
```

Seen in every gate from round 2 on during the #218 soak (one stack, ten runs of the suite).

## Done when

- Each run of the spec reads a bin no earlier run wrote to.
- The spec passes twice in a row against one stack (`make test-e2e ONLY=webhooks` run twice).

issues.title: Load test the API and live editing with k6
issues.body:
## Goal

Know how many concurrent users one Stator deployment carries before reads, writes or the worker slow down, and notice when a change makes that worse.

## Scope

- k6 scripts under `tests/load/`, run in the `grafana/k6` container through a `make test-load` target (nothing installed on the host). The k6 image is pinned to an exact version.
- Runs against the compose stack, signing in test users through the existing test endpoints rather than the browser login.
- Seed data: a space with a few thousand pages in a deep tree, attachments, comments, so lists and search are not trivially small.
- Scenarios, each with its own thresholds (p95 latency and error rate):
  - **Readers**: open a space, walk the page tree, read pages, search.
  - **Editors**: save drafts, publish, comment, with some editing the same page to exercise version conflicts.
  - **Live editing**: many clients on one page's collaboration socket.
  - **Mixed**: the realistic blend of the above, ramped up until thresholds break, to find the ceiling.
- The run writes a summary (requests per second, p50/p95/p99, errors per route) to a file that can be compared between runs.
- A short `docs/load-testing.md`: how to run it, what the scenarios model, the numbers measured on the reference stack, and what to look at when a threshold breaks (database pool, replica lag, worker queue depth).

## Not in scope

- Running the full ramp in the push gate or on every CI run. A short smoke version (a few users, one minute) may run in CI on demand via `workflow_dispatch`.
- Tuning whatever the test finds; findings become their own issues.

## Done when

- `make test-load` runs every scenario against a fresh stack and fails when a threshold is exceeded.
- The documented ceiling for the reference stack is measured, not guessed.

issues.title: Search checks permission on every page before it matches the words
issues.body:
## Problem

Search takes about 0.5 s per statement in a space of 2,000 pages, and every search runs two (the count and the page of hits), so `GET /search` answers in about 1.1 s at the median and 2.9 s at p95, at a load of three readers. Found by the k6 load test (#368).

## Cause

`EXPLAIN ANALYZE` of the page branch, as `stator_app` with a tenant set, for a word 108 of 2,001 pages hold:

```
Seq Scan on page p (actual time=9.716..506.599 rows=108 loops=1)
  Filter: (... org_id = current tenant ... AND perm_page_viewable(id, ...) AND search_vector @@ ...)
  Rows Removed by Filter: 1893
```

Row level security puts the policy's quals ahead of the query's, and `@@` is not `LEAKPROOF`, so the GIN index on `search_vector` cannot narrow the rows first: `perm_page_viewable` runs for every page of the organization, about 0.25 ms each. Search time grows with the size of the organization, not with the number of hits. The attachment and comment branches have the same shape.

## Done when

- A search for a word a few dozen pages hold answers well under the load test's threshold (p95 < 800 ms) in a space of 2,000 pages, measured with `make test-load`.
- The permission check runs for the matching pages only, and an integration test still proves a reader never sees a page they may not view, straight through SQL.

issues.title: The page tree of a large space checks permission page by page
issues.body:
## Problem

`GET /spaces/{key}/outline` takes about 0.8 s for a space of 2,000 pages, at a load of three readers. Found by the k6 load test (#368).

## Cause

The recursive query walks the tree and calls `perm_page_viewable(p.id, user)` for every page, at about 0.4 ms each, so the whole tree costs time in proportion to the space's size. The logged statement:

```
WITH RECURSIVE tree (...) AS (
  SELECT ... FROM page p WHERE p.id = $1
  UNION ALL
  SELECT ... FROM page p JOIN tree t ON p.parent_id = t.id
  WHERE p.trashed_at IS NULL AND p.archived_at IS NULL AND perm_page_viewable(p.id, $2::uuid)
)
SELECT id, parent_id, title, depth FROM tree ORDER BY path
```

Most of the work repeats: a page with no restriction of its own inherits its parent's answer, which the walk has just computed.

## Done when

- The outline of a 2,000-page space answers with p95 < 1 s under `make test-load`, and well under that alone.
- Restricted branches are still left out for whoever may not view them, proven by the existing tests and one through SQL.

issues.title: nginx opens a new connection to the api for every request and runs out of ports
issues.body:
## Problem

At about 250 requests per second through nginx, requests fail with 502: nginx cannot open a connection to the api.

```
[crit] connect() to 172.29.0.10:8080 failed (99: Address not available) while connecting to upstream
```

Found by the k6 load test (#368): the ceiling profile without search and the page tree reached 418 people at 246 requests/s with reads at p95 17 ms and writes at 73 ms, and then 242 requests failed this way within a second. The api and the database were nowhere near their limit.

## Cause

nginx speaks HTTP/1.0 to the api and closes the connection after every request, so each request takes a fresh local port, and each closed one waits in TIME_WAIT. At a few hundred requests a second the ephemeral ports run out. Both `deploy/nginx.conf` (compose, `proxy_pass $api` through a variable, which rules out a keepalive pool) and the chart's `configmap-nginx.yaml` (a fixed `proxy_pass`, but no `upstream` block) have no keepalive to the api.

## Done when

- nginx reuses connections to the api (an `upstream` block with `keepalive`, `proxy_http_version 1.1` and an empty `Connection` header for plain requests; WebSockets keep their upgrade), in compose and in the chart.
- The compose stack still survives the api container being recreated, which is why the variable is there.
- `make test-load LOAD_PROFILE=ceiling LOAD_SKIP=search,tree` gets past 250 requests/s without a 502, and docs/load-testing.md records the new ceiling.

issues.title: A client hanging up is logged as an internal server error
issues.body:
## Problem

When a client hangs up before its answer is ready, the api logs `level=ERROR msg="request failed" code=internal_error error="context canceled"` and counts a 500, although nothing failed on the server's side. nginx records the same requests as 499. Seen in bulk when a k6 load run (#368) stopped: 44 such errors in one second.

## Cause

`asValidationError` in `backend/internal/httpapi/request.go` turns `context.Canceled` into `ErrInternal`, the same as a database failure.

## Done when

A request whose client went away is logged at a lower level as cancelled by the client, not counted as a server error, and a test proves it. A deadline the server itself hit stays an error.

issues.title: One organization per instance: remove multiple organizations
issues.body:
## Decision

One Stator instance serves one organization. Whoever needs a second organization runs a second instance. The ability to hold several organizations in one instance goes away.

## Why

- Every table, policy, URL and test carries an organization it does not need for the way Stator is run: one team, one installation.
- Fewer moving parts: no organization switcher, no organization in links and sign-in, no tenant to set on every transaction.
- Separate instances keep organizations apart by separate databases and buckets, which is a stronger wall than row level security in one database.

## What it touches (to be planned before any code)

- **Database**: the `org` table becomes the instance's single settings row; `org_id` columns, the tenant isolation policies and `current_org_id()` go entirely, with no fixed value kept as an interim step (decided 2026-10-12). The access policies (viewers, restrictions, anonymous readers) stay; only the tenant part goes. An existing instance with more than one organization is refused by the upgrade with a message saying how to proceed: export every organization, delete organizations until one is left, then upgrade.
- **API and web**: `/auth/switch-org`, organization slugs in public links, sign-in (`/auth/oidc/{orgSlug}/start`) and anonymous URLs (`/public/{orgSlug}/...`), the organization switcher, bootstrap settings (`STATOR_BOOTSTRAP_ORG_*`).
- **Armature**: how an instance names itself to Armature and the stub, and linked accounts.
- **Tests**: the browser suite isolates every spec in a throwaway organization (`POST /test/orgs`). It needs another way to keep specs apart in one instance, such as a space and people per spec, and the integration tests that prove tenant isolation are removed or replaced.
- **Backup** (#108) and the chart: unchanged in shape, simpler in what they hold.
- **docs/decisions.md**: replaces "Multi-tenant by organisation, enforced by the database" (2026-09-29).

## Done when

- A fresh instance has exactly one organization and no way to make a second; nothing in the UI or the API names an organization to choose.
- An existing instance with one organization upgrades in place; one with several is refused with a message telling the operator to export every organization, delete all but one, and upgrade again; a test proves the refusal.
- No `org_id` column, tenant policy or `current_org_id()` is left in the schema.
- Every access guard still holds and is proven through SQL as before; the tenant guards are gone with their tests.

issues.title: Compare load test runs with a committed baseline
issues.body:
## Goal

Notice when a change makes Stator slower, even while it stays under the load test's fixed thresholds (#368): search going from 30 ms to 400 ms still passes a p95 < 800 ms threshold.

## Scope

1. **A committed baseline.** `tests/load/baseline.json` holds the standard profile's numbers from the reference machine named in `docs/load-testing.md`: p50, p95 and p99 per kind of request (read, write, search, tree), live delivery and opening a shared draft, requests per second and the failure rate. It changes only on purpose, in the pull request that changes performance, with the reason in its description.
2. **A comparison.** `make load-compare` runs the standard profile against the running stack and compares its summary with the baseline. It fails when a p95 grows by more than a margin (25 % to start, a named constant) or the failure rate rises, and prints a table of baseline, now and change for every number. `make load-baseline` writes a new baseline from a run, for the pull request that means to change it.
3. **When it runs.** Before a release (a step in the release checklist) and on pull requests that touch queries, permissions or live editing, by hand. Not in the push gate or the PR gate.
4. **Optional:** a nightly scheduled run of the Load workflow that uploads its summary as an artifact, failing nothing, for a rough trend. Shared runners are no reference machine, so it never gates.

## Not in scope

- Committing the result of every run.
- Gating pull requests on load numbers from shared runners.

## Done when

- `make load-compare` passes against the committed baseline on the reference machine, and fails when a regression is planted (a test or a documented check, such as sleeping in a search).
- `docs/load-testing.md` says when to run it, how to read its table, and how and when to update the baseline.

## Proposal

## Problem

The sidebar's bottom left shows `0.1.0`: the web build reads the `VERSION` file (`web/vite.config.ts`) and nothing else. It does not say which commit is running, so two different builds look the same, and it lacks the `v` people expect of a release. - The web image and the backend images take the version and commit from the same build arguments (compose, the chart's images, CI), so the page and the api never disagree; a build outside git falls back to the `VERSION` file with no hash.

## Done when

- The bottom left shows `vX.Y.Z` for a tagged build and `vX.Y.Z+<short hash>` otherwise, in both themes and on mobile, and stays accessible.
- The api reports the same version and commit (for example in `/readyz` or a small version endpoint), and a test checks the page and the api agree in the compose stack.

issues.title: chore: release by tag the same way in all three tools

All three tools release the same way, following the release script of [chaosflix-jellyfin](https://github.com/praetorianer777/chaosflix-jellyfin/blob/main/release.sh) and its tag workflow:

issues.title: feat: give the webhook envelope a version
issues.body:
The webhook envelope carries a version, so its format can change without breaking receivers silently:


- A receiver ignores unknown fields and topics, and refuses an envelope version it does not know with a clear status and log line, instead of misreading it.
- The format is described in the OpenAPI document (or a JSON schema next to it) and covered by a contract test on both sides.
